fields.headline: STATE PICKS PARAVISION FOR DIGITAL ID
fields.deck: A five-year contract worth up to $6.5 million was awarded Sept. 23.

stories.caption:
The U.S. State Department has awarded facial recognition developer Paravision a firm-fixed-price contract worth up to $6.5 million. Federal procurement records describe the work as "digital detection/identity assurance."

The contract was signed September 23, with $1.3 million obligated at the start, and can run through September 22, 2031. The department filed the buy as a small-business set-aside under simplified acquisition rules, and only one bid came in.

Public award records do not name the Paravision products the department bought. The description overlaps with deepfake and synthetic-face detection technology that Paravision markets for protecting digital identity systems, but the record does not show whether the award includes that product, its liveness detection, facial recognition or other software. Earlier this year, on April 30, the department made a separate $24,717 purchase order to the company for a software license, and records do not show whether that was a test or pilot.

Source: Biometric Update, October 17, 2026

Image: Biometric Update (courtesy)

fields.headline: XTEND GETS $40.5M ORDER FOR STRIKER
fields.deck: XTEND advances to Gauntlet III after ranking as a top performer in Close Quarters Battle.

stories.caption:
XTEND AI Robotics, the Tampa-based company listed on the NYSE as XTND, has won a $40.5 million order for 6,000 STRIKER systems. The order follows the company's ranking among the top performers in the close quarters battle category of Gauntlet II, a stage of the U.S. Department of War's Drone Dominance Program.

STRIKER runs on XTEND's proprietary XOS operating system and is built for tactical missions in confined, complex and GNSS-denied environments. XTEND says it moves straight into Gauntlet III in the same category, part of Phase 3 of the program, which the department opened on September 28, 2026. Gauntlet II awardees must first fulfill a 400-system production order. Performance in Gauntlet III will decide whether any Phase 3 orders are placed, and the company stresses that taking part does not guarantee an award.

The company also released preliminary third quarter 2026 revenue figures and an update on its backlog.

Source: XTEND AI Robotics via Business Wire, October 13, 2026

fields.headline: ARMY TO TEST COUNTER-DRONE GEAR IN AFRICA
fields.deck: Selected systems would reach Soldiers within 180 days, the Army said.

frames.mediaQuery: counter-drone Soldiers African Lion 2026 Tan-Tan Morocco

stories.caption:
The U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF) is working with the Army's Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate (G-TEAD) to test emerging systems on the continent, with the goal of getting proven tools into Soldiers' hands quickly.

The command's first accelerated capability event (ACE) is planned for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. Its focus is defending early-entry command posts and operating locations against Group 1–3 small UAS, a gap the Army says is hard to close on training ranges in the United States and Europe. Army officials say Africa's open spectrum and uncongested airspace let Soldiers validate solutions in theater before scaling them across the service.

Next year's timeline runs in stages: a Soldier-led demonstration in Tan-Tan during February and March 2027, then an operational assessment in April and May during African Lion 2027. G-TEAD will validate up to 15 solutions with PAE Fires as the transition partner.

Source: U.S. Army, 16 October 2026

fields.story_03: Florida Guard tests drone data link

stories.caption:
MilCityUSA's ICYMI quick brief covers three stories published in the past week: Microchip's acquisition of Austin-based VORAGO Technologies, Lockheed Martin's PAC-3 Edge interceptor debut, and the Florida National Guard's Drone Crucible 26.3 integration test.

Microchip Technology's deal adds radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors and the HARDSIL process technology to its space and defense portfolio. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Lockheed Martin unveiled PAC-3 Edge as its entry in the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor competition. The company says testing is planned for 2027, with deployment targeted by 2031.

The Florida National Guard's exercise at Camp Blanding linked Tactical Assault Kit location data, unmanned-system information and video feeds into one shared operational picture, and the Guard said dedicated specialists were critical to keeping it working.
